title: Open-world progression — natural Level 1 through E class evolution
brief: Start a genuine Level-1 campaign. Make becoming a capable Guild adventurer your central motivation: choose contracts, exploration, combat, loot sales, equipment and skill development freely. Play until the Engine confirms Level 15 AND your chosen E class evolution; death, genuine blockers and technical safety limits remain separate endings. At sensible town visits sell surplus loot, seek affordable weapon/armour upgrades and supplies, buy useful upgrades and equip them. Keep needed gear, supplies and quest cargo; revisit shops when money or stock changes. Allocate earned stats and pursue real learning or training. Recover, including sleep, before danger, assess enemy strength and numbers, and choose easier work or withdraw when sensible. Quests, routes, tactics and build remain yours. Incidental NPC help, relationships, paid work and detours are welcome; do not seek private errands as your main occupation. Note optional blockages and choose alternatives. No forced fights, farming, scripted routes, fixtures or invented accomplishments. Input 100 is a comparison checkpoint, not the finish.

milestones.goal: Create a genuine Level-1 character with your own base class and starter-skill choices. For this AoE comparison choose one of your two starter skills as Cleave (Warrior), Arcane Wave (Mage), or Fan of Blades (Rogue); choose the other freely. Use AoE only when tactically useful, checking the target band and possible friendly fire; withdraw or choose easier work when needed.
Develop your freely chosen Level-1 character through real play until the Engine confirms Level 15. Keep improving gear and skills; then continue to class evolution instead of stopping.

After Level 15, finish pending danger, inspect #class/#feats and freely choose an offered E class. Panels are read-only; if the offer is due, take a safe ordinary story turn. Normal is valid: never farm Rare. Only Engine-confirmed acceptance finishes this milestone; no E fight is required.

focus: Observe whether Guild progression, loot sales, equipment upgrades, recovery and skill growth are useful and engine-confirmed in your freely chosen adventures.
Note meaningful contradictions and failed actions even when you can work around them. Keep messages concise and use panels only to resolve uncertainty.
personas: independent cautious Guild adventurer: choose suitable contracts, prepare, recover, sell surplus loot and improve equipment and skills
curious Guild adventurer: freely explore and choose interesting contracts while developing levels, gear and techniques; incidental help remains welcome
pragmatic Guild adventurer: value achievable contracts, loot sales and useful gear or skill investments without reckless fights
